undergoing an evaluation for kidney retransplantation and 
possible mitral valve repair, coming in for scheduled left and

 She is not currently on hemodialysis. She has been hoping to 
avoid dialysis and is in the process of finding a living donor. 
.
Patient, on admission, was complaining of decreased exercise 
tolerance and shortness of breath, with transient chest 
discomfort that occurred on exertion and at rest, most times 
when she was lying supine.  Patient noted that over the past few 
months she has had significantly decreased exertional capacity, 
which has been progressive, in which she gets fatigued from 
walking from her driveway to her house.  She has been able to do 
ordinary activities of daily living without major difficulty.  
She reported associated chest discomfort on exertion, described 
as a pinching, wringing feeling that lasts less than a minute 
and goes away.  The discomfort is located in the ___ her 
chest.  She also noticed the same feeling when laying down at 
night to go to sleep, and noted significant multiple pillow 
orthopnea.  This feeling tended to last longer, more than one 
minute and then went away.  There was no associated nausea, 
diaphoresis or palpitations.  Patient stated that she felt 
'fluid overloaded', and endorsed a 'gurgling' feeling in her 
chest when lying flat as well.  She also reportd a 'whooshing' 
sound in her ears.
.  
On review of systems, she denied any prior history of stroke, 
TIA, deep venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, bleeding at the 
time of surgery, myalgias, joint pains, cough, hemoptysis, black 
stools or red stools. She denied recent fevers, chills or 
rigors. She denied exertional buttock or calf pain. All of the 
other review of systems were negative.  
.  
Cardiac review of systems was notable for absence of paroxysmal 
nocturnal dyspnea, palpitations, syncope or presyncope.
.
On admission, patient reported no chest pain, dyspnea, 
palpitations, abdominal pain, or dysuria.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old female with history of coronary artery disease s/p 
NSTEMI ___ with DES to the RCA and PDA, moderate to severe 
mitral regurgitation, T1DM s/p kidney and pancreas transplant x 
2, peripheral vascular disease, currently undergoing an 
evaluation for kidney retransplantation and mitral valve repair, 
and coming in for scheduled left and right heart catheterization 
with TEE.

ACTIVE ISSUES
-------------
# Coronary artery disease: patient presented for hydration, in 
preparation for left and right heart catheterization as well as 
transesophageal echocardiogram.  Patient reported no chest pain 
at the time of admission.  Patient has two stents in the right 
coronary artery, one in the posterior descending artery from 
previous catheterziations.  She is not on Plavix due to concern 
for bleeding after previous endoscopies, and currently is only 
on aspirin 81 mg PO daily, which was continued on admission.  
Patient experienced chest pain when laying flat on the night 
after admission, responsive to one sublingual nitroglycerin and 
not associated with ECG changes or cardiac biomarker elevations. 
 Her carvedilol and amlodipine dose was increased due to 
hypertension during her hospital course.  Her lisinopril was 
stopped due to her worsened renal function noted below.  Her 
rosuvastatin was continued during her hospitalization.  It was 
elected by the patient not to undergo catheterization during 
this admission, since it would probably mean that the patient 
would have to be on dialysis afterwards.  The plan is to have 
the patient follow up with Dr. ___ as an outpatient to further 
discuss further management.  She was discharged on increased 
doses of carvedilol and amlodipine, along with a prescription 
for sublingual nitroglycerin to be used if she has chest pain.  
Patient has follow up scheduled with Dr. ___ 
cardiologist, and her PCP/nephrologist after discharge.
  
# Mitral regurgitation: moderate to severe on last transthoracic 
echocardiogram, but was likely underestimated.  Catheterization 
was to be performed as part of evaluation for mitral valve 
replacement.  Patient reported, on admission, of being 
symptomatic with dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, and peripheral 
edema while at home.  She was also found to have an elevated 
JVP.  Patient was hypertensive during her first day of admission 
and carvedilol dose was increased as well as her amlodipine.  
Her home dose of lisinopril was discontinued due to acute kidney 
injury.  Patient will follow up with Dr. ___ to further 
discuss mitral valve repair in the future.

# Acute on chronic kidney disease s/p kidney transplant: patient 
is on tacrolimus, sirolimus and prednisone, and is chronic 
kidney disease stage V status post deceased donor renal 
transplant in ___ with subsequent allograft failure.  She is 
currently awaiting living donor transplant, and was reluctant to 
undergo dialysis.  Baseline creatinine was reportedly 2.6-3.2 
prior to admission, with admission creatinine being 3.9, 
representing acute kidney injury.  Cardiac catheterization was 
postponed due to high risk of renal failure and permanent 
hemodialysis.  Patient was continued on her home dose of 
tacrolimus, sirolimus and prednisone and daily tacrolimus levels 
were checked.  Renal transplant ultrasound was performed and 
showed no acute abnormality.  Urine electrolytes showed FEUrea 
of 40, representing interstitial injury.  Nephrotoxins were 
avoided, lisinopril was discontinued, and medications were 
renally dosed.  She was continued on calcium and Vitamin D 
supplementation.  Nephrology was consulted and patient stated 
that she refuses dialysis at the current time.  She will follow 
up with her PCP, who is also a nephrologist, for further 
management.

# Hypertension: patient was hypertensive soon after admission.  
Her carvedilol and amlodipine dose was increased due to 
hypertension during her hospital course.  Her lisinopril was 
stopped due to her worsened renal function noted below.  Patient 
was continued on her home hydralazine.  She will resume 
increased doses of carvedilol and amlodipine, as well as his 
home dose of hydralazine.

INACTIVE ISSUES
---------------  
# Rhythm analysis: patient was monitored on telemetry, and 
patient remained in normal sinus rhythm during her admission.
  
# Diabetes mellitus type 1: patient is status post pancreas and 
kidney transplant, and has not been on any therapy.  She was 
continued on her home dose of tacrolimus, sirolimus and 
prednisone, and daily tacrolimus levels were trended. 

# Hyperlipidemia: patient was continued on her home dose of 
rosuvastatin, which she should continue as an outpatient, goal 
LDL<70.

# Anemia: etiology likely secondary to kidney disease.  Patient 
did not require transfusion during hospitalization, and her 
hematocrit remained stable during hospitalization.

radiology_notes.text:
PORTABLE CHEST, ___

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  Heart size remains normal.  Lungs are clear except for a small
linear area of atelectasis in the right mid lung.  No pleural effusion.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of pulmonary edema.

INDICATION:  A ___ female with acute kidney insufficiency, elective
cardiac catheterization, status post renal transplant from ___.

COMPARISON:  Renal transplant biopsy, ___ and renal transplant
ultrasound ___.

FINDINGS:  The transplant kidney is again seen in the right lower quadrant and
measures 12.3 cm.  A mild amount of perinephric fluid is noted.  No
hydronephrosis is seen.  The renal pelvis and proximal ureter are noted to be
echogenic in appearance, which could suggest a fungal UTI with urothelial
thickening or possibly redundant urothelium secondary to chronic dilatation as
a result of distention of the bladder.  No focal abnormality is seen in the
transplant kidney.  The bladder is only minimally distended and demonstrates
mild wall thickening.

DOPPLER EXAMINATION:  Color Doppler and pulse-wave Doppler images were
obtained.  Appropriate arterial waveforms with sharp upstrokes are seen in the
main renal artery.  Appropriate venous flow is seen in the main renal vein. 
Resistive range from 75 to 78.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Trace of perinephric fluid in the right lower quadrant.  No
hydronephrosis.  Thickening of the renal pelvis and proximal ureter could
represent redundant urothelium based on frequent distention of the bladder or
could represent a fungal UTI with urothelial thickening.  Clinical correlation
for fungal UTI is suggested.
2.  Mild thickening of the bladder wall is noted.
3.  Patent transplant kidney vasculature.
